title: Extract information from video · Level 2
slo: Describe the information a video analyzer can extract from a meeting.

exercises.question_text: What total attendee count was returned for the conference-room image?

options.rationale: This is correct. One in-person attendee plus three remote attendees gives four total attendees.

options.error_type: Confuses total attendees with in-person attendees
options.rationale: This is incorrect. One is the in-person count and omits the remote attendees.
options.better_fit: Use this when asked specifically for the in-person attendee count.

feedback.intrinsic: The meeting would appear much smaller than the returned total.
feedback.instructional: Add one in-person attendee and three remote attendees.

options.error_type: Confuses total attendees with remote attendees
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Three is the remote-attendee count and omits the in-person attendee.
options.better_fit: Use this when asked specifically for the remote attendee count.

feedback.intrinsic: One attendee would be left out of the count.
feedback.instructional: The total includes both remote and in-person attendees.

options.rationale: This is incorrect. The reported parts are one in person and three remote, which total four.
options.better_fit: This would fit only if the separate attendee counts added to five.

feedback.intrinsic: The attendance record would overcount the meeting.
feedback.instructional: Use the reported parts: one plus three equals four.

exercises.explanation: Correct—one in-person attendee plus three remote attendees equals four.

exercises.question_text: prebuilt-videoSearch is selected when the input is video.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The recorded video would not be matched to its intended analyzer.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Select prebuilt-videoSearch when the input is video.

exercises.explanation: Correct—the analyzer matches the video input.

exercises.question_text: A video meeting schema can record attendance counts at different ___.

parts.text: A video meeting schema can record attendance counts at different

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The results would not show when attendance changed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use time intervals for attendance changes over a recording.

exercises.explanation: Attendance can change as a meeting continues. Time intervals allow the schema to record those changes at different points in the video.

exercises.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A colleague might not understand how the results support later work.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with structured results, then connect their storage, search, analysis, and downstream use.

exercises.correct_answer: Structured results can be stored, searched, analyzed, and passed to downstream systems.
exercises.explanation: Structured results support storage, search, analysis, and downstream use. The order forms one clear statement of these connected uses.

exercises.question_text: A supervisor reviews a recorded meeting because people joined and left during the call. Which field should the supervisor include to see how attendance changed?

options.rationale: This is correct. Counts at time intervals show attendance at different points in the recording.

options.error_type: Confuses video-over-time tracking with a still-image result
options.rationale: This is incorrect. One total gives a single count and cannot show people joining or leaving over time.
options.better_fit: Use this when one overall count is sufficient for a single image.

feedback.intrinsic: The supervisor could not see attendance changes.
feedback.instructional: Use counts at different time intervals when attendance changes over a recording.

options.error_type: Confuses video schema with invoice schema
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Tax amount is an invoice field and provides no meeting-attendance information.
options.better_fit: Use this when extracting billing information from an invoice.

feedback.intrinsic: The review would contain a billing amount instead of attendance history.
feedback.instructional: Choose the meeting field: attendance counts at time intervals.

options.error_type: Confuses video schema with voicemail schema
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A caller email address is a voicemail contact field and does not track meeting attendance.
options.better_fit: Use this for a recorded voice message when extracting contact details.

feedback.intrinsic: The supervisor would still not know when people joined or left.
feedback.instructional: Attendance changes require time-based counts, not contact details.

exercises.explanation: Correct—time-interval counts show how attendance changes.

exercises.question_text: A meeting coordinator wants summaries and assigned actions from recorded meetings to trigger later workflow steps. What should the coordinator pass to the workflow system?

options.rationale: This is correct. Structured JSON results carry summaries and assigned actions into later automation.

options.error_type: Confuses source media with extracted output
options.rationale: This is incorrect. The raw video is source content and does not organize summaries and actions into structured fields.
options.better_fit: Use this as the input to video analysis.

feedback.intrinsic: The workflow would not receive ready-to-use meeting details.
feedback.instructional: Pass structured JSON results after analysis, not only the source video.

options.error_type: Confuses a source image with structured media results
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A camera image is source content and does not contain the extracted meeting summary and actions.
options.better_fit: Use this to identify location and attendee counts from a conference-room image.

feedback.intrinsic: The workflow would miss the meeting summary and assigned actions.
feedback.instructional: Use structured JSON results when later steps need extracted meeting information.

options.error_type: Confuses a schema definition with analysis results
options.rationale: This is incorrect. An invoice schema defines potential invoice fields; it is not extracted meeting results.
options.better_fit: Use this when defining fields for invoice analysis.

feedback.intrinsic: The workflow would receive field definitions instead of meeting outcomes.
feedback.instructional: A schema describes what to extract; structured JSON results contain the extracted information.

exercises.explanation: Correct—structured JSON results can be passed to downstream systems for automation.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The counts would be difficult to interpret.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the image result, then state the in-person count, remote count, and total.

exercises.correct_answer: The image returned one in-person attendee three remote attendees and four total.
exercises.explanation: The result identifies the image report, then gives the in-person count, remote count, and total. This order makes the attendance breakdown clear.

exercises.question_text: The prebuilt analyzer for video analysis is ___.

parts.text: The prebuilt analyzer for video analysis is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The video could be sent to an analyzer for a different content type.

exercises.explanation: prebuilt-videoSearch is the prebuilt analyzer identifier for video. Its name distinguishes it from audio, image, and invoice analyzers.

exercises.question_text: A facilities manager checks a conference-room camera image after a meeting. Which results should the manager use to understand attendance? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. It shows how many attendees were physically present.
This is correct. It shows how many attendees joined remotely.
This is correct. It provides the combined attendance count.

options.error_type: Confuses meeting-image fields with voicemail fields
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A caller email address is contact information and does not measure meeting attendance.
options.better_fit: Use this for a recorded call when extracting callback contact details.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would have contact information but no attendance measure.
feedback.instructional: Attendance comes from the in-person, remote, and total counts.

exercises.explanation: Correct—these three fields describe attendance in the image.

exercises.question_text: A recorded meeting can be analyzed as ___ content.

parts.text: A recorded meeting can be analyzed as

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The recording would be grouped with the wrong content type.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose video for a recorded meeting; audio, documents, and images fit other inputs.

exercises.explanation: A recorded meeting is video content. Video analysis extracts meeting-related information from that recording.

exercises.question_text: A developer is building an app to analyze a recorded meeting video and return structured information. Which choices fit the task? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. prebuilt-videoSearch is the prebuilt analyzer for video input.
This is correct. The recorded meeting video is the content the analyzer is designed to process.
This is correct. Video analysis produces structured information related to the video.

options.error_type: Confuses video analysis with invoice analysis
options.rationale: This is incorrect. An invoice analyzer is designed for invoice content and does not match a recorded meeting video.
options.better_fit: Use an invoice analyzer when the input is an invoice and billing fields are needed.

feedback.intrinsic: The app would be set up for invoice details instead of meeting details.
feedback.instructional: For recorded video, select prebuilt-videoSearch and submit video input.

exercises.explanation: Correct—these choices match a video-analysis task.

exercises.question_text: A meeting coordinator has a recorded video conference and needs attendance, speakers, and assigned actions. Which analysis approach should the coordinator choose?

options.rationale: This is correct. Video analysis is the approach that can extract the requested meeting details from the conference recording.

options.text: Extract fields from a scanned invoice
options.error_type: Confuses meeting analysis with document extraction
options.rationale: This is incorrect. Invoice extraction provides billing information rather than meeting activity.
options.better_fit: Use this when extracting vendor, tax, totals, and other invoice fields.

feedback.intrinsic: Leaders would receive billing details instead of meeting details.
feedback.instructional: Use video analysis when the required information comes from a recorded conference.

options.error_type: Confuses video analysis with audio extraction
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A voicemail can provide call-related details, but it is not the recorded conference with visual meeting context.
options.better_fit: Use this for a call recording when a transcript, summary, or contact details are needed.

feedback.intrinsic: Attendance from the conference would remain unknown.
feedback.instructional: The relevant input is the recorded video conference, not an audio voicemail.

options.text: Extract purchase details from a receipt photo
options.error_type: Confuses video analysis with image extraction
options.rationale: This is incorrect. A receipt photo contains purchase information and cannot provide meeting participants or actions.
options.better_fit: Use this for expense descriptions and amounts from a receipt image.

feedback.intrinsic: The coordinator would have receipt details but no meeting outcomes.
feedback.instructional: Use video analysis for information contained in the meeting.

exercises.explanation: Correct—analyzing the recording as video meets the stated meeting-information need.
